seoTitle: How to Fix PayPal Trouble With This Transaction Error
metaDescription: Getting PayPal's 'We're having trouble with this transaction' message? Here's what PayPal's own decline reasons cover, and where to check which one is yours.
intro: PayPal's "We're having trouble with this transaction" message is one of the more frustrating errors you can hit mid-checkout, mostly because the wording gives no clue what went wrong. This guide walks through what the error looks like on screen, where PayPal actually tells you the real reason once you look past the alert, and how to work through the specific decline reasons PayPal itself documents before you retry the payment.

steps.heading: Recognize the error when it appears
steps.body: The message shows up as a full-screen alert with a warning icon, the "We're having trouble with this transaction" headline, and a smaller line suggesting you try again with another card. It's a generic screen, so the same alert appears whether the real cause is a declined card, an account hold, or a security check; the alert itself won't say which. Tapping OK just dismisses it and returns you to checkout, so the real work happens in your account, not on this screen.

image.caption: PayPal's generic transaction-error alert, the same message covers card declines, account holds, and security checks alike.

steps.heading: Check your notifications and the Resolution Center
steps.body: Log in to PayPal and open the notifications bell in the top right of the dashboard. PayPal's own help documentation points to this bell icon, or the Resolution Center, as the place account limitations and required actions actually surface. In a typical case you'll see items like "Identity verification is in progress" or a request to "provide your GST registration details," and either type of item can block a transaction without ever mentioning the checkout screen.

image.caption: The PayPal dashboard with the notifications panel open, showing an identity-verification hold and a GST registration request, either can trigger the transaction error.

steps.heading: Match your situation against PayPal's own decline reasons
steps.body: PayPal's help center lists a specific set of reasons a payment gets declined, most of which produce this same generic alert instead of a specific message. Work through the table below in order; it covers the documented causes from most to least common. New accounts and accounts with a thin transaction history tend to hit the security-check and unconfirmed-card items more often, since PayPal's risk checks lean harder on unfamiliar patterns.

steps.heading: Confirm your cards and bank account are properly linked
steps.body: Go to Banks & Cards in the left-hand menu to see every payment method tied to your account, including masked card numbers and linked bank accounts. If the card or account you're trying to pay with isn't listed here, shows as unverified, or has a "Confirm Card" link next to it that you haven't clicked, that matches two of PayPal's own decline reasons directly. Add, confirm, or re-link the correct method from this screen before retrying.

image.caption: The Banks & Cards page, listing a linked bank account and a Visa credit card, the place to confirm your payment method is recognized and confirmed before you retry.

steps.heading: Retry once the underlying issue is cleared
steps.body: Once you've cleared any notification, confirmed your card or bank account, and ruled out a spending limit or balance issue, retry the transaction. If PayPal asked for identity confirmation as part of a security check, complete that first; retrying before an open security check clears tends to reproduce the same generic error.

tables.title: PayPal's documented reasons a payment gets declined
rows: Declined by your bank or card issuer
Contact your card issuer or bank directly; PayPal isn't told the specific reason.
Update the expiration date or billing address on the card in Banks & Cards.
Open the Resolution Center and complete the steps listed for the limitation.
Confirm your identity when prompted; this verifies it's really you using the account.
Confirm the email address tied to your PayPal account in account settings.
Confirm the linked bank account before using it to pay.
Click "Confirm Card" next to the card in Banks & Cards if that link is showing.
tables.note: From PayPal's own "Why was my payment declined?" help article. PayPal shows the same generic transaction-error alert for most of these instead of naming the specific reason on screen.

troubleshooting.problem: The error keeps appearing even after checking notifications
troubleshooting.cause: An older, unresolved notification further down the list is still blocking payments, even after a more recent one has been handled.
troubleshooting.fix: Open the Resolution Center and clear every open item, not just the newest one.

troubleshooting.problem: A card shows in Banks & Cards but payments with it still fail
troubleshooting.cause: The card has never been confirmed, which is a separate status from simply being linked.
troubleshooting.fix: Look for a "Confirm Card" link next to that card and complete it before retrying.

troubleshooting.problem: The error happens specifically on large or unusual payments
troubleshooting.cause: PayPal's security check can flag a payment for identity confirmation when it looks unlike your normal activity.
troubleshooting.fix: Complete the identity confirmation PayPal requests before retrying, instead of repeating the same payment.

faq.question: Why does PayPal say it's having trouble with my transaction?
faq.answer: It's a generic error PayPal shows for several distinct problems: a card issuer decline, an account limitation, a required security check, an unconfirmed email or bank account, or a card that hasn't been confirmed. The alert itself doesn't say which.

faq.question: Does this error mean my account has been banned?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. PayPal's own decline reasons are mostly fixable issues, like an unverified card or a pending identity check, instead of a permanent ban.

faq.question: Where do I see why PayPal flagged my payment?
faq.answer: Open the notifications bell on your PayPal dashboard, or the Resolution Center directly, instead of relying on the error message. That's where PayPal lists specific holds and required actions.

faq.question: Can a new PayPal account cause this error more often?
faq.answer: Yes. Newer accounts face more frequent security checks and card-confirmation requirements, both of which are on PayPal's own list of decline reasons.

faq.question: What's the difference between a linked card and a confirmed card?
faq.answer: A card can appear in Banks & Cards as linked but still show a "Confirm Card" link, which PayPal separately requires before that card can be used to pay.

faq.question: Will contacting my bank help if PayPal declines the payment?
faq.answer: It can, for one specific reason on PayPal's list: if your bank or card issuer declined the payment, PayPal says it isn't told why, so the card issuer is the only one who can explain it.

verifiedNote: The error screen and dashboard screens come from a walkthrough recorded in 2025. The list of decline reasons and the Resolution Center's role were checked against PayPal's official Help Center in September 2026, replacing the article's earlier general guesses (currency mismatches, device or network changes) with PayPal's own documented reasons, which do not include those two as listed causes.
